_readme: The answer key for the eight KB documents in this directory.
Proposal 93 §5: KB documents must be 'real prose with answerable facts, or the
KB test is unfalsifiable'. A document alone cannot make a test falsifiable — a
suite that ingests eight documents and asserts 'a result came back' passes on
the wrong result. This file is the other half: for each question, the exact
strings that must appear in the retrieved chunk, and the document they must
come from.
WHY THE QUESTIONS LOOK LIKE THIS — retrieval is LEXICAL ONLY.
backend/services/rag.py:198 generate_embedding returns None unconditionally
('Knowledge-base search is TEXT-ONLY, deliberately' — owner decision
2026-08-17, no Google spend). The vector half of search_hybrid filters on
c.embedding IS NOT NULL and can therefore never match. Every question below
must survive websearch_to_tsquery on the 'english' configuration and share
stemmed terms with the document — a purely semantic paraphrase retrieves
nothing, and a question that fails for that reason is not evidence about the
knowledge base.
Titles carry tsvector weight A and content weight B (rag.py:132 _KB_TSV), so
`ingest_title` below is part of the fixture, not decoration. Use it verbatim.
unanswerable_questions exist so the suite can prove the KB says nothing rather
than inventing something. A KB that answers those is worse than one that
answers nothing.

client.name: Zanskar Medtech Limited
client.note: Invented. Ingest under a hub_clients row created for the run; hub_kb_documents.client_id is NOT NULL and the org is resolved from it (rag.py:276).

questions.q: What is the standard warranty period on a ZM-series analyser?
questions.why: Two competing periods in one sentence. An answer that gives only one of them has retrieved the chunk but read it wrong.

questions.q: What restocking charge applies to a return?
What format does an RMA number take and how long is it valid?
questions.why: An identifier format is impossible to answer by guessing.

questions.q: How much does the Gold service plan cost per year?
questions.why: Three plans with three prices in one chunk; the wrong one is a visible failure.

questions.q: What on-site response time does the Silver plan give?
questions.why: Distinguishes Silver from Bronze (5 days) and Gold (1 day) within one chunk.

questions.q: What ambient temperature range is required for installation?
questions.why: A range, so a half-right answer is detectable.

questions.q: What is charged for a wasted installation visit?
questions.why: One unusual number appearing exactly once in the corpus.

questions.q: What is the lead time for a ZM-1200X?
questions.why: Four lead times in one block; the model code disambiguates ZM-1200 from ZM-1200X.

questions.q: How quickly must transit damage be reported?
questions.why: Appears twice in the same document, so retrieval of either sentence answers it.

questions.q: What is the first response target for a P1 ticket?
questions.why: Three priorities in one chunk with three different targets.

questions.q: Who is level 3 in the escalation path?
questions.why: A named person the corpus mentions exactly once, so a hallucinated name is obvious.

questions.q: What is the price of part ZM-P-5513?
questions.why: A twelve-row price table. Retrieving the chunk is not enough; the right row must be read.

questions.q: How long are remote diagnostic logs retained?
questions.why: Five retention periods in one list; 13 months is the only one in months.

questions.q: Does Zanskar Medtech hold patient data?
questions.why: A negative fact. A KB that cannot answer a negative will answer this one wrongly rather than not at all.

questions.q: When does the warranty period start, according to the commissioning checklist?
expect_all: not from the date of despatch
questions.why: This fact lives in the SECOND chunk of the only multi-chunk document. If chunk 2 was never stored, this question is the one that fails — which is the point of including it.

questions.q: What outbound port must the instrument reach for updates?
questions.why: Deliberately spelled in words. Digits would be stripped differently by to_tsvector; this proves retrieval on ordinary prose rather than on a number.

unanswerable_questions.q: What is the calibration interval for the ZM-4000?
unanswerable_questions.why: There is no ZM-4000 anywhere in the corpus. The correct behaviour is to say so.
unanswerable_questions.measured_warning: This question SCORES 0.1319 against 08-commissioning-checklist and therefore CLEARS KB_MIN_SCORE (0.10). Measured on the live database 2026-08-29 with the exact ranking expression from rag.py. The retriever will hand a chunk to the model for a question the corpus cannot answer, so a suite that asserts 'no chunk returned' will FAIL here and a suite that asserts 'a chunk returned' proves nothing. Assert on the ANSWER TEXT: it must decline.

unanswerable_questions.q: Who is the auditor of Zanskar Medtech Limited?
unanswerable_questions.why: The corpus never names an auditor. A KB grounded on these eight documents cannot know.

unanswerable_questions.q: What is the mobile number of the Mysuru service manager?
unanswerable_questions.why: No telephone number in this corpus is a real number and none is a mobile. An answer here is a fabrication.

measured.how: A table-free SELECT on the live database reproducing rag.py's exact ranking — setweight(title,'A')||setweight(content,'B') scored with ts_rank(..., 32) against the ORed websearch_to_tsquery. No relation referenced, nothing written.
measured.result: Every answerable question ranked its own source document FIRST and cleared KB_MIN_SCORE. Correct-document scores: warranty period 0.2198, restocking 0.2590, RMA format 0.1593, Gold price 0.2325, Silver response 0.2085, commissioning-date warranty start 0.2085, outbound port 0.1685.
caveats: Scores were computed on the FULL document text. Ingested chunks are smaller, and ts_rank rises as the matched document shortens, so live chunk scores should be at or above these. This is a floor, not a prediction.

The threshold does not discriminate on its own. 'What is the standard warranty period' clears 0.10 against TWO documents (0.2198 and 0.1352) and an off-corpus question clears it against one. Rank order is what separates them, so assert on which document came back, not on whether one did.

known_risk.what: KB_MIN_SCORE is low enough to pass an unanswerable question
known_risk.note: Measured, not suspected — see unanswerable_questions[0].measured_warning. This is a finding about the threshold, not about the fixture, and it is the reason every assertion here is on answer text rather than on result count.
